name: Ninja Database
tagline: Kellerman Software's commercial embedded object/relational database for .NET, Xamarin and Unity apps.
description: Ninja Database Pro is a compact (about 220 KB) embedded database written in C# that stores .NET objects either inline as embedded children or in separate related tables, so it acts as an object store or a lightweight relational store depending on how you model child objects. It provides ACID transactions with automatic rollback on the next open, LINQ index queries, paging, constraints, triggers, foreign keys, LRU caching, AES encryption and LZO compression, and copes with class changes through automatic schema evolution. It targets .NET Framework, .NET Standard and Core, Mono, Xamarin, UWP and Unity, with a cheaper Lite edition. Kellerman Software still sells it, but updates have slowed to occasional fixes; the latest NuGet release is 3.20.0 from January 2023.
statusNote: Still sold by Kellerman Software, but only bug-fix updates since 2019; latest release 3.20.0 (Jan 2023).

pricing.notes: Developer, team and site licenses, optionally with source code; trial available.

strengths: Zero-configuration: tables and indexes are created from your classes automatically
Automatic schema evolution when properties are added, removed or retyped
Built-in AES encryption and compression in a ~220 KB assembly
One API across desktop .NET, Xamarin mobile, UWP and Unity
weaknesses: Closed source unless you buy a source license
Development has slowed to occasional fixes
No SQL, no server mode and a small user community
useCases: Local storage for Xamarin or .NET MAUI-era mobile apps
Desktop .NET apps that want object persistence without an ORM
Unity games storing structured save data
